region: Dundee · Seneca Lake, Finger Lakes, New York
about: Glenora was the first winery on Seneca Lake. It was founded in 1977 by three local grape growers, Gene Pierce, Eastman Beers and Edward Dalrymple, with businessman Howard Kimball, and opened in May 1978. Pierce and his partners also helped pass New York’s Farm Winery Act, which let small wineries sell directly to visitors. Glenora later added a restaurant and an inn on its west-shore hillside, and in 2025 the property was acquired by Lilly Broadcasting, led by brothers Brian and Kevin Lilly.

Cabernet Sauvignon is a challenge this far north, and Glenora makes it from some of the warmest sites around the lake. In the most recent technical sheet available (2020), the fruit came mostly from the Welliver family’s Mason Road vineyards on Seneca’s east side, with small amounts of Cabernet Franc and Merlot. The wine was fermented warm on its skins for about ten days and given gentle oak. Head winemaker Edward Miller has led the cellar since 2021.

The 2023 won a Gold Medal and 90 points from the Beverage Testing Institute, which described black currant, graphite, garden soil and wild strawberry, with dried plum and black tea on the finish, and called it a Cabernet with New World fruit and Old World balance. At 12.2% alcohol, it is a lighter, food-friendly take on the grape.
facts: Cabernet Sauvignon (the 2020 was 94%, with Cabernet Franc and Merlot)
Mainly the east side of Seneca Lake (per the 2020 sheet)
